title: Phrasal Verbs with Away and Back: Leaving, Returning and Responding
summary: Use phrasal verbs with away to describe leaving, escaping, avoiding, discarding and storing things. Use back to describe returning, replying, repaying, responding and remembering. Place pronoun objects correctly and distinguish similar verb combinations by meaning.
learningObjectives: Contrast movement away from a person or place with coming or going back to a previous location.
Choose accurately among get away, get away with and keep away from in situations involving escape, wrongdoing and safety.
Distinguish give away, throw away, put away and give back, placing pronoun objects between a separable verb and its particle.
Use call back, get back to somebody, pay back and look back on to discuss communication, money and past experiences.

explanation.heading: Away and back express opposite directions
explanation.body: Away describes movement from a place or person, or time spent somewhere else. Back describes a return to a previous place, person or situation. Go away can mean leave home for a period; get back, come back and go back describe returning. Add a destination with to where needed: go back to the office, but get back home. A verb such as look away can describe moving your attention rather than physically leaving.
explanation.example: The family went away for the weekend and got back late on Sunday.

explanation.heading: Escaping, avoiding consequences and staying at a distance
explanation.body: Get away means manage to leave or escape, especially when leaving is difficult. Get away with something means do something wrong without being caught or punished: the preposition with is essential. Keep away from someone or something is a warning not to approach; from introduces the danger or person. These are different meanings, even though they share away.
explanation.example: The visitor ignored the rule and got away with it because nobody noticed.

explanation.heading: Giving, discarding, storing and removing things
explanation.body: Give something away means donate it or hand it to someone without expecting it back. Throw something away means discard it as unwanted; put something away means store it in its usual place. Take something away means remove it from a particular place. These verbs are normally separable: with a pronoun, say give it away, throw it away, put it away or take it away, never give away it.
explanation.example: We put the reusable decorations away and threw the damaged ones away.

explanation.heading: Returning items and replying to other people
explanation.body: Give something back means return it to the previous owner. Put something back means restore it to its former position, while take something back can mean return a purchase to a shop. Call somebody back means return a telephone call; get back to somebody means reply or provide information later, by phone, message or another method. In a separable expression, say call her back and give it back. Get back to her keeps to because it is part of a different pattern.
explanation.example: I could not answer the client immediately, so I got back to her the next morning.

explanation.heading: Repayment, reciprocal responses and looking into the past
explanation.body: Pay somebody back or pay money back means repay money that was borrowed. A wave, smile, shout or message can be returned with wave back, smile back or write back. Look back on a period or event means think about it after some time has passed; on introduces what you are remembering. These uses of back are not necessarily about physical movement.
explanation.example: Years later, Mei looked back on her first concert with pride.

comparisons.title: A permanent gift versus a returned loan

left.label: give away
left.example: Tariq gave his old bicycle away to a neighbour.
left.note: The bicycle becomes somebody else’s because Tariq no longer wants to keep it.

right.label: give back
right.example: Tariq gave the borrowed bicycle back to his neighbour.
right.note: The bicycle is being returned to the person who owned it.

comparisons.title: Two different meanings of get away

left.label: get away
left.example: The frightened deer got away before anyone approached.
left.note: The deer managed to escape or leave.

right.label: get away with
right.example: The player got away with breaking the rule.
right.note: The player avoided detection or punishment for wrongdoing.

left.label: put away
left.example: Please put the winter blankets away until next year.
left.note: The blankets are kept for future use.

right.label: throw away
right.example: Please throw the torn packaging away.
right.note: The packaging is unwanted and will be discarded.

comparisons.title: Returning a phone call versus replying more generally

left.label: call somebody back
left.example: I called Dani back after missing her call.
left.note: A new phone call responds to an earlier phone call.

right.label: get back to somebody
right.example: I got back to Dani by email the following afternoon.
right.note: A response can be provided through different communication channels.

examples.sentence: The visitors drove away from the campsite before sunrise.
examples.note: Drove away describes movement from a starting location.

examples.sentence: We will be back at the guesthouse before dinner.
examples.note: Be back describes being at the previous place again.

examples.sentence: The puppy managed to get away through an open gate.
Keep away from that loose fence panel.
examples.note: Keep away from is a warning to remain at a safe distance.

examples.sentence: I am giving these spare notebooks away because I no longer need them.
examples.note: Give away means transfer unwanted items to somebody else, not return borrowed ones.

examples.sentence: The children put their puzzles away after the game.
examples.note: Put away describes placing things where they are normally stored.

examples.sentence: I borrowed her charger, so I must give it back this evening.
examples.note: The pronoun it must come between give and back.

examples.sentence: We called the restaurant back to confirm the booking.
examples.note: Call back means return a telephone call.

examples.sentence: I will pay you back on the first day of next month.
examples.note: Pay somebody back means repay borrowed money.

examples.sentence: Looking back on that summer, I remember how much we learned.
examples.note: Look back on introduces reflection about an earlier experience.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I threw away it after opening the parcel.
commonMistakes.correct: I threw it away after opening the parcel.
commonMistakes.why: With separable throw away, an object pronoun must appear between the verb and the particle.

commonMistakes.incorrect: She got away breaking the rules without a warning.
commonMistakes.correct: She got away with breaking the rules without a warning.
commonMistakes.why: Get away with something requires with when it means avoid the consequences of wrongdoing.

commonMistakes.incorrect: Could you call back me after lunch?
commonMistakes.correct: Could you call me back after lunch?
commonMistakes.why: Call back is separable; the object pronoun goes between call and back.

commonMistakes.incorrect: The supplier has not got back for me yet.
commonMistakes.correct: The supplier has not got back to me yet.
commonMistakes.why: Use get back to somebody when you mean respond to a message or request.

commonMistakes.incorrect: I look back my first year at university with affection.
commonMistakes.correct: I look back on my first year at university with affection.
commonMistakes.why: Look back on a period or event requires on before the thing remembered.

studyTips: Draw a simple direction map: away = from a place; back = returning. Add a destination with from or to only where the verb pattern needs it.
Make two columns for unwanted objects: put it away means keep it; throw it away means discard it. Add give it away and give it back to contrast ownership.
Practise separable phrasal verbs with pronouns: give it back, throw them away, call her back, pay him back.
Learn fixed combinations as chunks: get away with, keep away from, get back to, and look back on. Each following preposition changes or completes the meaning.

exercises.prompt: After borrowing the headset for a meeting, Felix ___ it to its owner.
exercises.feedback: Gave back means returned something that belonged to someone else; gave away means donated it.

exercises.prompt: The old kettle belonged to us, but it was broken beyond repair, so we decided to ___.
exercises.feedback: Throw it away means discard an unusable item. The pronoun belongs between throw and away.

exercises.prompt: The dog escaped through a hole in the fence before its owner could catch it. It ___.
exercises.feedback: Got away describes a successful escape from a place or person.

exercises.prompt: I emailed the landlord with a question yesterday. I hope she will ___ soon.
exercises.feedback: Get back to somebody means reply to a question or message.

exercises.prompt: After the workshop, Priya ___ the paintbrushes in their usual cupboard. (put away; past simple)
exercises.feedback: Put away means store the paintbrushes in the place where they belong; the past form of put is put.

exercises.prompt: I cannot speak now. I will ___ after the presentation. (call + you + back)
exercises.feedback: Call somebody back means return a phone call, and the pronoun you goes before back.

exercises.prompt: The railing is loose, so please ___ it. (keep away from)
exercises.feedback: Keep away from means remain at a safe distance from a dangerous object.

exercises.prompt: The hikers ___ from their four-day trip yesterday. (get back; past simple)
exercises.feedback: Got back means returned from a period away; the past tense of get is got.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: After using the folding chairs, the assistants put away them in the storeroom.
acceptedAnswers: After using the folding chairs, the assistants put them away in the storeroom.
exercises.feedback: With pronoun them, put away requires the pronoun between the verb and particle.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: Please call back me tomorrow afternoon.
acceptedAnswers: Please call me back tomorrow afternoon.
exercises.feedback: Call back is separable; put the pronoun me between call and back.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The student got away copying the answers because nobody saw him.
acceptedAnswers: The student got away with copying the answers because nobody saw him.
exercises.feedback: Get away with an action means avoid being caught or punished; it requires with.

exercises.prompt: Correct the sentence: The agency has not got back for me about the application.
acceptedAnswers: The agency has not got back to me about the application.
exercises.feedback: Use get back to somebody for replying, not get back for somebody.

speakingExercises.prompt: You borrowed a book and will return it. Say one complete sentence beginning with "I" and using will (or I’ll) + give it back. Do not add a time or recipient.
speakingExercises.feedback: Give it back means return a borrowed item; place it before back.

speakingExercises.prompt: Correct the pronoun position and say the full sentence without changing any other words: "Please put away them before dinner."
acceptedAnswers: Please put them away before dinner.
speakingExercises.feedback: The pronoun object must come between put and away.

speakingExercises.prompt: You missed your colleague’s call. Say one sentence beginning with "I" and using will (or I’ll) + call you back after lunch. Do not add other words.
acceptedAnswers: I'll call you back after lunch.
I will call you back after lunch.
speakingExercises.feedback: Call you back means make a return phone call, with you before back.

speakingExercises.prompt: A gust of wind carried a loose ticket away. Say one past-simple sentence using exactly these ideas: The ticket / blow away. Begin with "The ticket".
speakingExercises.feedback: Blew away means the wind carried the ticket from where it was.

speakingExercises.prompt: A customer emailed you on Monday. You replied on Tuesday. Say one past-simple sentence beginning "I" and using got back to the customer on Tuesday.
acceptedAnswers: I got back to the customer on Tuesday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Got back to describes replying to a person, in this case on Tuesday.

speakingExercises.prompt: Address children directly to warn them about an unsafe machine. Say exactly one imperative sentence using Keep / away from / the machine. Do not mention the children.
speakingExercises.feedback: Keep away from is a clear instruction to remain at a safe distance.

speakingExercises.prompt: Produce exactly two past-simple sentences from these facts. First: Sam / go away / on Friday. Second: Sam / come back / on Sunday. Begin both sentences with "Sam".
acceptedAnswers: Sam went away on Friday. Sam came back on Sunday.
speakingExercises.feedback: Went away describes leaving; came back describes the later return.

speakingExercises.prompt: Aisha is reflecting on her first job. Use only these words, changing the verb to the present simple: Aisha / look back on / her first job.
acceptedAnswers: Aisha looks back on her first job.
speakingExercises.feedback: Look back on an experience means think about it from a later point in time.

listeningExercises.audioText: Nadia borrowed a tablet for a training session, but she gave it back before lunch.
listeningExercises.prompt: What happened to the borrowed tablet?
listeningExercises.feedback: Gave it back means returned the tablet to its owner.

listeningExercises.audioText: We cancelled the picnic because of the rain, so I put the folding chairs away in the shed.
listeningExercises.prompt: Why did the speaker store the chairs?
choices: The chairs were broken beyond repair.
listeningExercises.feedback: The rain caused the cancellation, and put away describes storing the chairs.

listeningExercises.audioText: The children ran away when they heard a sudden loud bang.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the two-word verb phrase immediately after "The children".
listeningExercises.feedback: Ran away describes leaving quickly, often because of fear.

listeningExercises.audioText: The shop charged me twice by mistake, but they paid me back the following morning.
listeningExercises.prompt: How did the shop correct its mistake?
listeningExercises.feedback: Paid me back means returned money owed to the customer.

listeningExercises.audioText: The contestant broke the rules, but nobody noticed, so he got away with it.
listeningExercises.prompt: What happened after the contestant broke the rules?
listeningExercises.feedback: Got away with it means he escaped detection or punishment for breaking the rules.

listeningExercises.audioText: I emailed the organiser on Monday. She got back to me on Wednesday with all the details.
listeningExercises.feedback: Got back to me means replied, and the response came on Wednesday.

listeningExercises.audioText: The ranger warned visitors to keep away from the unstable cliff edge.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the three-word expression immediately after "to".
listeningExercises.feedback: Keep away from tells someone to avoid going near a dangerous place.

listeningExercises.audioText: When Omar looks back on his school days, he remembers his kind teachers.
listeningExercises.prompt: Type the three-word expression immediately after "Omar".
listeningExercises.feedback: Looks back on is used for reflecting on past experiences.
